videos.title: Nvidia Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
videos.description:
"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Suzan DelBene says there should be an investigation into Nvidia and Jensen Huang to understand potential national security implications. Kevin Brady, former Republican Congressman from Texas, says Democrats are effectively in control of the timing and content of government funding legislation during the lame-duck session as control of the House changes hands. Gregory Allen, Founder and CEO of Decision Tree Research, says Nvidia is not structured to easily absorb the loss of Jensen Huang and argues the company has been built around Huang’s leadership without a clear successor. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Jensen Huang should be subpoenaed if he does not appear for a requested voluntary interview with lawmakers.

videos.title: Brady Says Democrats Control Lame-Duck Funding Timing
videos.description:
Kevin Brady, former Republican Congressman from Texas, says Democrats are effectively in control of the timing and content of government funding legislation during the lame-duck session as control of the House changes hands. Brady says he expects lawmakers to extend government funding rather than allow a shutdown, although the timing remains unsettled. Brady says divided government could create opportunities for bipartisan tax policy, including IRS reforms and changes related to the 2025 tax law. Brady says Democrats are also likely to pursue restoration of renewable-energy, child and health-care tax credits while proposing higher taxes on corporations and individuals. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power."

videos.title: CoreWeave Earnings Triggers AI Boost
videos.description:
CoreWeave shares jumped after the company eased fears about its debt-laden business and signaled strong sales growth despite headwinds facing the data center boom. Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Brody Ford reacts to the earnings report. Plus, Anthropic’s initial public offering has drawn multiple times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz previews next weeks expected mega-IPO. Then, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Rachel Metz talks OpenAI’s quarterly revenue, which hit $10 billion for the first time, driven by strong demand for its latest artificial intelligence software. We also hear from Bloomberg Senior Editor for Tech & Strategic Industries Michael Shepard on federal investigations into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy. Finally, Bloomberg News Sustainability Editor Eric Roston breaks down how climate models missed on key predictions.

videos.title: LIVE: Millions of Spaniards stage first general strike in 14 years over housing
videos.description:
A view of Madrid as four million Spanish workers took part in a general strike, unions said, enduring stormy weather to set up picket lines in a protest against the country's housing affordability crisis less than three weeks before a snap general election.

It ‌is the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis. The walkout is backed by Spain's two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, representing more than a million workers, as well as tenants' associations angry about rising rents and evictions.

videos.title: How NIL Deals Are Turning High-School Sports Into Big Business | WSJ
videos.description:
Amateur athletes’ ability to sign endorsement deals that monetize their name, image, and likeness has pumped billions of dollars into college sports. Now it’s coming for high school athletes. 

For some parents and coaches, NIL deals create welcome opportunities for students to offset the growing costs of elite youth sports. Others, especially in the six states that still restrict NIL activity before college, think allowing teenage athletes to cash in on their personal brands takes the increasing professionalization of amateur sports too far.

videos.title: HBCUs and the World Bank Group: A Global Partnership
videos.description:
A Shared Mission, A Global Vision for Transforming Lives and Strengthening Economies

What happens when two institutions with a shared commitment to transforming lives and communities come together to advance global development?

Historically Black Colleges and Universities have a distinguished legacy of developing global leaders, advancing scientific discovery, fostering entrepreneurship, and driving economic and social transformation in the United States and around the world. Building on this legacy, collaboration brings together HBCUs' talent, research capabilities, innovation, and global networks with the World Bank Group's development expertise and global reach to create jobs, strengthen economies, and advance shared development priorities.

In this conversation, IFC Vice President Elena Bourganskaia and Xavier University of Louisiana President Dr. C. Reynold Verret explore how the World Bank Group and HBCUs can leverage education, innovation, and entrepreneurship to create jobs, strengthen economies, and expand opportunity, building on a legacy of service and translating shared commitments into lasting development impact.

ABOUT THE WORLD BANK 🌐 The World Bank is one of the world’s largest sources of funding and knowledge for low-income countries. Its five institutions share a commitment to reducing poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development on a livable planet. http://www.worldbank.org

videos.title: How AI Is Changing Jobs in East Asia and Pacific | Regional Economic Update
videos.description:
How can artificial intelligence (AI) create better jobs, raise productivity, and increase incomes in East Asia and Pacific?

Watch the replay as World Bank economists Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby, co-authors of the October 2026 East Asia & Pacific Economic Update, explore how AI is changing jobs and skills across the region, how businesses can adopt AI, and what countries can do to ensure more workers benefit from a changing labor market.

The discussion explores:
- How businesses can adopt AI in ways that fit local needs
- How AI is changing the skills employers seek
- What policies can expand AI adoption and its economic benefits
Omar Arias and Patrick Kirby answered audience questions during the program, while Alessandro Barattieri, a co-author of the Economic Update, answered questions in the live chat.

Explore more resources and read the October 2026 East Asia & Pacific Economic Update: https://live.worldbank.org/en/event/2026/regional-economic-update-harnessing-ai-for-better-jobs-in-east-asia-and-pacific?cid=ECR_YT_worldbank_EN_EXT

videos.title: From Local Prices to the Global Economy: The International Comparison Program
videos.description:
How do we compare economies beyond exchange rates? Purchasing power parities (PPPs) provide a clearer picture of global development, poverty, and inequality. The International Comparison Program, or ICP, is one of the world’s largest statistical collaborations—bringing together a multitude of agencies and experts to measure and compare economic activity across nearly 200 economies. Learn how the ICP is shaping the future of global economic measurement—ensuring that better data leads to better policies, smarter investments, and more informed decisions worldwide. 

Learn more:
